Pilgrims come to San Miguel del Milagro to visit the sanctuary of the Archangel Michael. According to local religious tradition, he appeared to Diego Lázaro in 1631; this story gave rise to the veneration of the site and its spring.

The church stands on elevated ground in the state of Tlaxcala. Its relatively small interior preserves examples of religious painting and woodcarving. The sanctuary makes a suitable pilgrimage stop on the route between Mexico City, Tlaxcala and Puebla, while attending Mass offers an opportunity to experience its living religious tradition.

San Pablo Lake makes you want to interrupt your journey and step down to the water. The lake lies near Otavalo in Imbabura Province, in northern Ecuador. The volcano of the same name rises above it: its broad slopes fill much of the horizon, while passing clouds alternately reveal and conceal its upper reaches.

A walk along the shore lets you take in the Andean scenery at an unhurried pace. The light changes across the water, and fields and settlements are visible beyond the lake. Find a spot with an open view, listen to the wind and linger to see the same summit from several angles. San Pablo is especially striking when the clouds leave patches of sunshine on the slopes.

The lake is an easy addition to a visit to the area around Otavalo. After the market and artisan towns, a stop here gives you time to enjoy the region's natural scenery. You can walk by the water or relax with views of the volcano; ask locally which water activities are available. San Pablo appeals to travellers who love sweeping mountain panoramas and are happy to adjust their plans for beautiful light.

## Moon Valley and the El Tatio Geysers: What to See in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile

San Pedro de Atacama! You can visit Moon Valley, where dunes display an extraordinary range of colours. In the Sacred Reserve, you will see the Three Marys rock formation. Crossing the Siloli Desert, you will be captivated by Laguna Colorada, where flamingos nest, the thermal waters of Polques, Licancabur Volcano and the Sun Geysers.

The Chilean village of San Pedro de Atacama lies in the heart of one of the world's driest deserts, the Atacama. Travellers from around the globe are drawn to the archaeological site of Tulor, where numerous remarkable artefacts have been discovered. San Pedro de Atacama is also one of the few places in the country where you can try genuine chilli peppers. They grow here in arid conditions, which makes them exceptionally hot.

## History and Nature in San Pedro de Atacama

### The Most Extraordinary Landscapes Around San Pedro de Atacama!

The village's main landmark is the Church of San Pedro, built in the 17th century. Along the main street, Caracol, you will find numerous souvenir shops selling handmade goods. The spectacular surroundings also deserve special attention: the El Tatio geysers, the Altiplano lagoons, Moon Valley and the Atacama Salt Flat.

A beautiful lakeside village that attracts people who enjoy a healthy, active lifestyle. You can practise your Spanish, learn to play African drums or simply stretch out in a hammock.

## Relaxing in San Pedro La Laguna

### San Pedro La Laguna — A Little Piece of Paradise in Guatemala!

San Pedro La Laguna is the starting point for climbs up the many volcanoes in the surrounding area. The lake itself is remarkable for its exceptionally clear water, reflecting the nearby volcanoes and the blue sky. At the many cafés, you can enjoy a delicious meal as well as a cup of fragrant coffee.
